A ciascun’alma presa e gentil core
O voi che per la via d’Amor passate
Piangete, amanti, poi che piange Amore
Ballata i’ voi che tu ritrovi Amore
Tutti li miei penser parlan d’Amore
Con l’altre donne mia vista gabbate
Ciò che m’incontra, ne la mente more
Spesse fiate vegnomi a la mente
Amore e ’l cor gentil sono una cosa
Ne li occhi porta la mia donna Amore
Voi che portate la sembianza umile
Se’ tu colui c’hai trattato sovente
Donna pietosa e di novella etate
Io mi senti’ svegliar dentro a lo core
Tanto gentile e tanto onesta pare
Li occhi dolenti per pietà del core
Venite a intender li sospiri miei
Era venuta ne la mente mia
Videro li occhi miei quanta pietate
Color d’amore e di pietà sembianti
Gentil pensero che parla di vui
Lasso! per forza di molti sospiri
Oltre la spera che più larga gira
Lo doloroso amor che mi conduce
Voi che ’ntendendo il terzo ciel movete
Amor che ne la mente mi ragiona
Poscia ch’Amor del tutto m’ha lasciato
Amor, che movi tua vertù dal cielo
Io son venuto al punto de la rota
Al poco giorno e al gran cerchio d’ombra
Amor, tu vedi ben che questa donna
Così nel mio parlar voglio esser aspro
Tre donne intorno al cor mi son venute
Doglia mi reca ne lo core ardire
Qual che voi siate, amico, vostro manto
Savere e cortesia, ingegno ed arte
Non mi poriano già mai fare ammenda
Guido, i’ vorrei che tu e Lapo ed io
Volgete li occhi a veder chi mi tira
Deh ragioniamo insieme un poco, Amore
Com più vi fere Amor co’ suoi vincastri
De gli occhi de la mia donna si move
Ne le man vostre, gentil donna mia
Di donne io vidi una gentile schiera
- Voi, donne, che pietoso atto mostrate
Un dì si venne a me Malinconia
Chi udisse tossir la mal fatata
Ben ti faranno il nodo Salamone
Bicci novel, figliuol di non so cui
Parole mie che per lo mondo siete
Due donne in cima de la mente mia
Chi guarderà già mai sanza paura
Io Dante a te che m’hai così chiamato
I’ ho veduto già senza radice
Perch’io non trovo chi meco ragioni
Se vedi li occhi miei di pianger vaghi
Io sono stato con Amore insieme
Degno fa voi trovare ogni tesoro
Io mi credea del tutto esser partito
Per quella via che la bellezza corre
Anzi che Amore nella mente guidi
Quai son le cose vostre ch’io vi tolgo
Se non si move d’ogni parte amore
Amor, sì come credo, ha signorìa
Deh moviti, Pietate, e va’ incarnata
Uomo, lo cui nome per effetto
L’uom che conosce è degno c’haggia ardire
Gli occhi vostri gentili e pien d’amore
In sin che gli occhi miei non chiude morte
Lo fin piacer di quello adorno viso
Poscia ch’io vidi gli occhi di costei
L’alta speranza, che mi reca Amore
Come non è con voi a questa festa
Or dov’è, donne, quella ’n cui s’avvista
Giovine bella, luce del mio core
Gli atti vostri li sguardi e ’l bel diporto
Il mio cor, che ne’ begli occhi si mise
Amor, che ha messo ’n gioia lo mio core
Quando Amor gli occhi rilucenti e belli
Nelle man vostre, o dolce donna mia
Quand’io pur veggio che se ’n vola ’l sole
Se conceduto mi fosse da Giove
Amor, la dolce vista di pietate
La bella donna, che ’n virtù d’Amore
Una donna mi passa per la mente
Lasso! che, amando, la mia vita more
Questa donna che andar mi fa pensoso
Angel di Dio simiglia in ciascun atto
Tutto mi salva il dolce salutare
Egli è tanto gentile et alta cosa
Veduto han gli occhi miei sì bella cosa
Poi che saziar non posso gli occhi miei
Se questa gentil donna vi saluta
Se ’l viso mio alla terra s’inchina
Ahimè! ch’io veggio ch’una donna viene
Ben dico certo che non fu riparo
Non v’accorgete, donna, d’un che smuore
Io sento pianger l’anima nel core
Ahi lasso!, ch’io credea trovar pietate
Non credo che ’n madonna sia venuto
Udite la cagion de’ miei sospiri
Questa leggiadra donna che io sento
Tu che sei voce che lo cor conforte
Tanta è l’angoscia c’haggio dentro al core
Guardate, amanti! io mi rivolgo a vui
Guarda crudel giudicio che fa Amore
O tu Amor che m’hai fatto martire
Amor, la doglia mia non ha conforto
La grave udienza degli orecchi miei
Se non si muor, non troverà mai posa
O giorno di tristizia e pien di danno
Vinta e lassa era già l’anima mia
Quando potrò io dir Dolce mio Dio
Sì m’ha conquiso la selvaggia gente
Cecco, io ti prego per virtù di quella
Li più begli occhi che lucesser mai
Quando l’anima trista e ’l corpo e ’l core
Lo gran disio, che mi stringe cotanto
Onde ne vieni, Amor, così soave
La bella stella che ’l tempo misura
Mille volte ne chiamo il dì mercede
Dante, io non odo in quale albergo suoni
Di nuovo gli occhi miei per accidente
Donna, io vi miro; e non è chi vi guidi
Novellamente Amor mi giura e dice
Poi ch’io fui, Dante, dal mio natal sito
Occhi miei, deh fuggite ogni persona
Ciò ch’io veggo di qua m’è mortal duolo
Io guardo per li prati ogni fior bianco
Deh!, non mi domandar perch’io sospiri
Dante, io ho preso l’abito di doglia
Signor, e’ non passò mai peregrino
Da poi che la natura ha fine ’mposto
L’alta virtù, che si ritrasse al cielo
Ciò che procede di cosa mortale
Mille dubbi in un dì mille querele
Nel tempo della mia novella etate
Su per la costa, Amor, dell’alto monte

The Book of the Tavern Keeper (Sakiname)
“Oh! Red Rose,” said the Nightingale, “thee I’ll throne in love apart!”
If a sweet Turkish maid I know
Tavern Keeper, lo!--the moonrise on the fast of Ramazan!
God and I, and a good heart yet!
Now, Singer, a song that is fresh forsooth!
In The Market where the gamesters
Two and seventy sects are fighting--
In my merry mood of drinking
By the apple of your chin there
Tears, tears, wild tears, rend not I pray
Since now from the heart of night the rose
Of that dear day when first we met--Oh! Heart’s Delight,--
Come, Tavern Keeper, fill the glass!
When the evening call to prayer rings
From my love’s far dwelling to me
Within the mystic mosque there prays
I am thirsty for thine eyes, Love,
When The Tavern Keeper gives you a glass winking at the brim,
From The Book of Noble Living I would read a verse to thee,
When the merry wine-sun rising in the cup begins to glow,
At the Grave of His Son
Whate’er fate God’s given, take it!
Who’s never sown the seeds of love,
Great God, to whom in vain no one does pray,
See how on the cheeks of the tulip
Oh! kiss well and drink well,
The Eye of Mighty Love cares not
Thy face bathe well in water,
Praise God, the wine door’s open, Men!
A cozy nook, a maid to love, a mind that’s free from care,
Devout be in the daylight and drink thy wine by night,
Oh that Youth’s glowing gown must fade!

Some damsel I saw, supremely fair
Your hair dismays the yak, the mountain sinks into the vale
Which of the gods this fair face fashioned?
Why did that moon-face cross my path?
Fair-face, red brow-spot, there-behind the heavy
She left the shrine at cowdust-time, passing gliding
I could not see her clearly
Beholding that my love was at her bath
A joyous day this day for me!
Rāi of the lily face had not yet climbed the bank
She smiled a little when she saw me lurking there
The flower is open all amidst the thorns
Childhood and youth are mingled both
Day by day her breasts grew great.
Now and again her eyes to their corners fly
Childhood and youth are face to face,
The little buds are peeping shyly
How shall I tell of Kānu's beauty, my dear?
I had desired to look on Kānu
A peerless beauty I beheld, my dear
How can I tell the limits of my grief, my dear?
Happy is your birth, and blest your beauty!
Hearken fair damsel, to good advice
Now hear me, daughter of a king
I know not the taste of love, nor the colour of desire
Leave me, dear maid, I pray you,
When first the damsel to her leman came
The sakhī soothed her fears, and led her lovingly,
Ah damsel fair! in dalliance is no delight
How can I tell of what was done that night?
What can I say, my sakhī? It is shame to tell
Do not urge me, dearest maiden, do not urge.
O maiden, dearest maiden, do not lead me to him
Her gentle words she can but stammer
Oh Hari, Why do you seek to loose my girdle?
You that are skilled in passion's lore have pity
You are that Banamāli that did slay Chānur
Amorous the swain, and little is his darling
Enough! and cast the trouble from your heart.
O Hari, if you will insist on touching me
How to direct the flying arrows of her restless eyes
With soft persuasion all the maidens
Gainlier than a royal olifant, more graceful than the swan
The night is late, the fair one timorous and fearful
She veils her face, that lady shene,
The citizens are waking on the king's highway
Came the lord of seasons,--Royal Spring
In Brindāban renewed the groves are green
Drunken are the honey-bees in honey-season
The blissful night of Spring holds sway
He who was wont to wanton with a flute, has cast away
One little moment of a day you keep your youth,
You shall not tell me otherwise, my dear
With hanging head, she writes upon the ground
Your high round breasts--like golden cups
Hearken, O Mādhava: Rādhā is waxen wilful,
At last, my dear, I see how Kāna is uncouth
There bloomed a flower of golden shene
The sun is in the East, the tide of night has ebbed
Beauty, of lineage and courtesy, without your eyes
Thirsting for fragrance I flew to the flower
The wrath of the wrathful fled afar
'Tell me, O Beauty, what were the night's delights.
Measureless virtue! whereso yearning bodies meet
What can I tell of to-day's affair my dear?
What shall I tell you, dear gay friend?
My frolicsome friend, what shall I say?
O mother mine, what can I say to-day!
My mother-in-law was asleep, and I lay in her lap
I was alone, and weaving garlands
To-day my awkward shame was far away
What can I say, my dear? 'Tis measureless!
Her wandering hair was mingled with the circle of her face
Shyāma is drunk with Madan's drowsy wine
If you would have my love, O Mādhava
Like to the tool that trims the jewels of her toes
The mournful beauty, gazing on Kānu's face
A sorry end to all my love, my dear
Why would you burn my body, O thou Bodiless?
Often, in meditation on the name of Mādhava
Where wanton Murāri is wont to sit
Hari has gone to Mathurā town.
Now Mādhav has gone to Mathurā town
Watching with streaming eyes the way her darling went
I am a girl on fire, in the temple bird-alone
Even the moon's cool rays are scorching-hot
Fresh flowers are springing by every cabin, brake and copse.
There is no limit to my woe, my dear!
Who says that Mādhava will come, my friend?
O Kān, I saw the tender she beside herself!
Making a promise to return 'To-morrow,' her lover went away,
Everyone praises the gifts of love
How many reproaches and scornful words of my elders
I never thought that love would break
Explain this all to Kānu, dearest friend
I am dying, am dying, I die indeed, my dear
After how long shall this sadness depart?
Speak to me, speak to me, dear, and tell me, O tell me
The day that Mādhava went his way
A river of tears is flowing from her eyes
Ah Mādhava, I come just now from seeing Rāi
Mādhava, lo, I have seen your lovely Rāi,
She turns her face away from looking on the moon.
There was a time my lover leaned above my face in bliss
Mādhava and the babe new-led in love,
Can I forget, my dear and gentle lady
When Hari comes to Gokula town
When my dear and blissful lover comes to my garth
When Kāna shall come to my house
I spent last night in bliss
How shall I tell of my boundless joy, my dear,
The hurt that the Lord of the Seasons erstwhile did me
Fate is now friendly for ever more!
Rare was that meeting of one with the other
A mirror in hand, a flower in my hair
What would you ask of my feelings, my dear,
Hearken, O Mādhava, what more can I say?
Frenzied tresses encircling her radiant face

Amor, c’hai visto ciascun mio pensiero
Donna, vano è il pensier che mai non crede

Non mi dolgo di te, né di me stessi

Do gościa (Jeśli darmo masz te książki...)
Do gościa (Nie pieść się długo z mymi książeczkami...)

Do Jana (Radzę, Janie, daj pokój przedsięwzięciu swemu...)
Do Jósta (Wiesz, coś mi winien; miejże się do taszki...)
Do Kachny (Pewnie cię moje zwierciadło zawstydzi...)
Do Marcina (A więc by ty, Marcinie, przed tym nie ugonił...)
Do Mikołaja Firleja (Jesliby w moich książkach co takiego było...)
Do Mikołaja Mieleckiego (Nie dar jaki kosztowny, ale co przemogę...)
Do miłości (Chyba w serce, Miłości, proszę, nie uderzaj...)
Do paniej (Co usty mówisz, byś w sercu myśliła...)
Do paniej (Imię twe, pani, które rad mianuję...)
Do paniej (Pani jako nadobna, tak też i uczciwa!)
Do Pawła (Dobra to, Pawle, możesz wierzyć, szkoła...)
Do Pawła (Pawle, rzecz pewna, u twego sąsiada...)
Do Stanisława (Co mi Sybilla prorokuje ninie?)
Epitafium dziecięciu (Byłem ojcem niedawno, dziś nie mam nikogo...)
Epitafium dziecięciu (Ojcze, nade mną płakać nie potrzeba...)
O tymże (Wczora pił z nami, a dziś go chowamy...)
Drugie Temuż (Hiszpany, Włochy i Niemce zwiedziwszy...)
Na hardego (Nie bądź mi hardym, chociaś wielkim panem...)
Na hardego (Nie chcę w tej mierze głowy psować sobie...)
Ofiara (Łuk i sajdak twój, Febe, niech będzie, lecz strzały...)
O fraszkach (Komu sto fraszek zda się przeczyść mało...)
O fraszkach (Najdziesz tu fraszkę dobrą, najdziesz złą i śrzednią...)
O gospodyniej (Starosta jednej paniej rozkazał objawić...)
O Hannie (Serce mi zbiegło, a nie wiem inaczej...)
O miłości (Próżno uciec, próżno się przed miłością schronić...)
O żywocie ludzkim (Fraszki to wszytko, cokolwiek myślemy...)
O żywocie ludzkim (Wieczna Myśli, któraś jest dalej niż od wieka...)
Z Anakreonta (Ciężko, kto nie miłuje, ciężko, kto miłuje...)
Z Anakreonta (Ja chcę śpiewać krwawe boje...)
Z Anakreonta (Kiedy by worek bogatego złota...)
Do Anny (Królowi rówien, a jeśli się godzi...)
Do Anny (Wczora, czekając na twe obietnice...)
Do doktora (Arcydoktorem cię zwać każdy może śmiele...)
Do doktora (Mówiłem ci, nie noś mi tych fraszek, doktorze...)
Do doktora (Nie mam ci zacz dziękować, mój miły doktorze...)
Do doktora (Nie trzeba mi się wiele dowiadować...)
Do doktora (Nie wiem, podobno li to co ku rozumowi...)
Do dziewki (A co wiedzieć, gdzie chodzisz, moja dziewko śliczna...)
Do dziewki (Daj, czegoć nie ubędzie, byś nawięcej dała...)
Do fraszek (Fraszki moje, coście mi dotąd zachowały...)
Do fraszek (Fraszki, za wszeteczne was ludzie poczytają...)
Do gospodarza (Rad się widzę u ciebie, gospodarzu miły!)
Do gościa (Bądź ptaka, bądź zająca szukasz po tym boru...)
Do Hanny (Na palcu masz dyjament, w sercu twardy krzemień...)
Do Jędrzeja (A cóż radzisz, Jędrzeju? Wszak mogę w twe uszy...)
Do Jędrzeja (Który mój nieprzyjaciel i człowiek tak srogi...)
Do Jósta (Twój mi brat, Jóstcie, powiada o tobie...)
Do Marcina (Filozofi, co nad nas uszy lepsze mają...)
Do Mikołaja Mieleckiego (Na swe złeś mię upoił, mój dobry starosta...)
Do paniej (Słyszcie, pani! Te fraszki, co teraz czytacie...)
Do przyjaciela (Jednego chcieć i nie chcieć to społeczność prawa...)
Do przyjaciela (Nie frasuj sobie, przyjacielu, głowy...)
Do tegóż (Albo z nas szydzisz, albo sam wiłujesz...)
Do Stanisława (Powiedz mi, gdzie się chowasz, bracie Stanisławie...)
Do wojewody (Nie są, wojewodo zacny, czasy po temu...)
Do Wojtka (I owszem, miły Wojtku, zjednaj się z tą panią...)
Do Wojtka (Pytasz, nie teszno li mię tak samego siedzieć?)
Dorocie z Michowa, żenie jego (Nie chciałam cię, mężu mój, zostać, twoja żona...)
Na lipę (Gościu, siądź pod mym liściem, a odpoczni sobie!)
Na tenże (Nie woła dziś przewoźnik: „Wsiadaj, kto ma wsiadać!)
Na tenże (To jest on brzeg szczęśliwy, gdzie na czasy wieczne...)
Na toż (Gładkość od ciebie, Wenus, ale nie trwa w mierze...)
O drugim (Co się wam widzi ten drugi?)
O fraszkach (Próżno mnie do dziewiąci lat swe fraszki chować...)
O miłości (Kto naprzód począł Miłość dziecięciem malować...)
Tegoż małżonce (Anna z Piłce, dwu mężu zacnych pochowawszy...)
Temuż (By Bóg duszę za duszę chciał od nas przyjmować...)
Z Anakreonta (Podgórski źrzóbku, czemu, patrząc krzywo...)
Z greckiego (Alkon patrząc na syna, kiedy go smok srogi...)
Z greckiego (Ani w młodej rozkoszy, ani w starej widzę...)
Z greckiego (By się wszytka nawalność morska poruszyła...)
Z greckiego (Nie sądź mię za umarłą, gościu mój miły...)
Z greckiego (Nie z Messany, nie z Argu tu, zapaśnik, stoję...)
Z greckiego (Nie znam się ku tym łupom: kto li to, szalony...)
Z greckiego (W tym grobie piękna Timas leży pogrzebiona...)
Do doktora (Fraszka a doktor — to są dwie rzeczy przeciwne...)
Do dziewki (Jeśli to rada widzisz, a życzysz mi tego...)
Do dziewki (Nie uciekaj przede mną, dziewko urodziwa...)
Do fraszek (Fraszki nieprzepłacone, wdzięczne fraszki moje...)
Do gościa (Gościu, tak jakoś począł, już do końca czytaj...)
Do gościa (Gościu, własną twarz widzisz przeważnej Dydony...)
Do gospodarza (Nie bądź gościem u siebie, wiedz, co się w cię wleje...)
Do Jana (Janie, cierp', jako możesz! Przyjdzie ta godzina...)
Do Jana (Jeśli stąd jaką rozkosz ma człowiek cnotliwy...)
Do Kachny (Choć znasz uczynność moję i chęć prawą czujesz...)
Do Kachny (Po sukni znam żałobę, znam i po podwice...)
Do Mikołaja Firleja (Mało na tym, że moje fraszki masz pisane...)
Do miłości (Długoż masz, o Miłości, frasować me lata?)
Do miłości (Gdzie teraz ono jabłko i on klinot drogi...)
Do miłości (Jam przegrał, ja, Miłości! — Tyś plac otrzymała...)
Do pana (Bóg tylko ludzkie myśli wiedzieć może...)
Do pana (Panie, co dobrze, raczy dać z swej strony...)
Do Pawła (Pawle, nie bądź tak wielkim panem do swej śmierci...)
Do Stanisława (Kto pija do północy, bracie Stanisławie...)
Do wojewody (Zamieszkałem do stołu twego, wojewoda...)

Pieśń II (Serce roście patrząc na te czasy!)

Pieśń XIII (O piękna nocy nad zwyczaj tych czasów...)
Pieśń XIV (Patrzaj, jako śnieg po górach sie bieli...)
Pieśń XV (Nie za staraniem ani prze mą sprawę...)
Pieśń XVI (Królom moc na poddane i zwierzchność dana...)

Pieśń XX (Miło szaleć, kiedy czas po temu...)

Pieśń XXV (Użałuj sie, kto dobry, a potłucz zawiasy...)
Pieśń I (Przeciwne chmury słońce nam zakryły...)
Pieśń II (Nie dbam, aby zimne skały...)

Pieśń IV (W twardej kamiennej wieży i za troistemi...)
Pieśń VI (Królewno lutnie złotej i rymów pociesznych...)
Pieśń VII (Słońce pali, a ziemia idzie w popiół prawie...)
Pieśń VIII (Nie frasuj sobie, Mikołaju, głowy...)
Pieśń X (Może kto ręką sławy dostać w boju...)
Pieśń XII (Nie masz, i po drugi raz nie masz wątpliwości...)
Pieśń XIV (Wy, którzy Pospolitą Rzeczą władacie...)
Pieśń XIX (Jest kto, co by wzgardziwszy te doczesne rzeczy...)
Pieśń XVI (Nic po tych zbytnich potrawach, nic po tym...)
Pieśń XVII (Niegodzien tego ten świat zawikłany...)
Pieśń XVIII (Ucieszna lutni, w której słodkie strony)
Pieśń XX (Jaką, rozumiesz, zazdrość zjednałeś sobie...)
Pieśń XXI (Srogie łańcuchy na swym sercu czuję...)
Pieśń XXII (Proszę, jesli sie z tobą co śpiewało...)
Pieśń XXIV (Niezwykłym i nie leda piórem opatrzony...)

غزل ۱ — آه ، تا کی ز سفر باز نیایی؟ بازآ (Ghazal 1)
غزل ۲ — کشیده عشق در زنجیر، جان ناشکیبا را (Ghazal 2)
غزل ۳ — راندی ز نظر، چشم بلا دیده ما را (Ghazal 3)
غزل ۴ — چند به دل فرو خورم این تف سینه تاب را (Ghazal 4)
غزل ۵ — تازه شد آوازه خوبی ، گلستان ترا (Ghazal 5)
غزل ۶ — من آن مرغم که افکندم به دام صد بلا خود را (Ghazal 6)
غزل ۷ — طی زمان کن ای فلک ، مژده وصل یار را (Ghazal 7)
غزل ۸ — خیز و به ناز جلوه ده قامت دلنواز را (Ghazal 8)
غزل ۹ — نرخ بالا کن متاع غمزه غماز را (Ghazal 9)
غزل ۱۰ — نبود طلوع از برج ما، آن ماه مهر افروز را (Ghazal 10)
غزل ۱۱ — بار فراق بستم و ، جز پای خویش را (Ghazal 11)
غزل ۱۲ — عزت مبردر کار دل این لطف بیش از پیش را (Ghazal 12)
غزل ۱۳ — منع مهر غیر نتوان کرد یار خویش را (Ghazal 13)
غزل ۱۴ — چیست قصد خون من آن ترک کافر کیش را (Ghazal 14)
غزل ۱۵ — هست امید قوتی بخت ضعیف‌حال را (Ghazal 15)
غزل ۱۶ — بر سر نکشت درتب غم هیچکس مرا (Ghazal 16)
غزل ۱۷ — بر قول مدعی مکش ای فتنه‌گر مرا (Ghazal 17)
غزل ۱۸ — ننموده استخوان ز تن ناتوان مرا (Ghazal 18)
غزل ۱۹ — خانه پر بود از متاع صبر این دیوانه را (Ghazal 19)
غزل ۲۰ — ساکن گلخن شدم تا صاف کردم سینه را (Ghazal 20)
غزل ۲۱ — کس نزد هرگز در غمخانه اهل وفا (Ghazal 21)
غزل ۲۲ — صد حیف از محبت بیش از قیاس ما (Ghazal 22)
غزل ۲۳ — بسیار گرم پیش منه در هلاک ما (Ghazal 23)
غزل ۲۴ — از کاه ، کهربا بگریزد به بخت ما (Ghazal 24)
غزل ۲۵ — ای سرخ گشته از تو به خون روی زرد ما (Ghazal 25)

My sweetest Lesbia, let us live and love
Though you are young, and I am old
I care not for these ladies
My love hath vowed he will forsake me
When to her lute Corinna sings
It fell on a summer's day
The cypress curtain of the night is spread
Thou art not fair, for all thy red and white
See where she flies enraged from me!
Blame not my cheeks, though pale with love they be
When the god of merry love
Mistress, since you so much desire
Your fair looks inflame my desire
Hark, all you ladies that do sleep!
Come, let us sound with melody, the praises
What patron could I choose, great Lord, but you?
Author of light, revive my dying sprite!
Where are all thy beauties now, all hearts enchaining?
Out of my soul's depth to Thee my cries have sounded
View me, Lord, a work of Thine
Bravely decked, come forth, bright day!
To music bent, is my retired mind
Tune thy music to thy heart
Most sweet and pleasing are thy ways, O God
Lift up to heaven, sad wretch, thy heavy sprite!
As by the streams of Babylon
Come, cheerful day, part of my life to me
Seek the Lord, and in His ways persever!
Jack and Joan they think no ill
All looks be pale, hearts cold as stone
Such days as wear the badge of holy red
Vain men, whose follies make a god of Love
Harden now thy tired heart, with more than flinty rage!
Where she her sacred bower adorns
Fain would I my love disclose
Dear, that I with thee might live
Good men, show, if you can tell
What harvest half so sweet is
Sweet, exclude me not, nor be divided
There is none, O none but you
Pined I am and like to die
So many loves have I neglected
Though your strangeness frets my heart
Come away, armed with love's delights!
A secret love or two I must confess
Her rosy cheeks, her ever-smiling eyes
Where shall I refuge seek, if you refuse me?
Since now these clouds, that lately over-cast
Oft have I sighed for him that hears me not
Now let her change and spare not!
Were my heart as some men's are, thy errors would not move me

Break now, my heart, and die! O no, she may relent

Shall I come, sweet love, to thee
Thrice toss these oaken ashes in the air
Be thou then my Beauty named
O sweet delight, O more than human bliss
Thus I resolve, and time hath taught me so
Come, O come, my life's delight
Could my heart more tongues employ
Sleep, angry beauty, sleep, and fear not me
Silly boy, 'tis full moon yet, thy night as day shines clearly
So quick, so hot, so mad is thy fond suit
Shall then hope when faith is fled?
On you th' affections of your father's friends
Respect my faith, regard my service past
Thou joyest, fond boy, to be by many loved
Veil, Love, mine eyes! O hide from me
Every dame affects good fame, whate'er her doings be
So sweet is thy discourse to me
To his sweet lute Apollo sung the motions of the spheres
Young and simple though I am
Love me or not, love her I must or die
What means this folly, now to brave it so
Dear, if I with guile would gild a true intent
O Love, where are thy shafts, thy quiver, and thy bow?
Beauty is but a painted hell
Are you, what your fair looks express?
Since she, even she, for whom I lived
Must I complain, yet do enjoy my love
Think'st thou to seduce me then with words that have no meaning?
Turn all thy thoughts to eyes
If any hath the heart to kill
Beauty, since you so much desire
Your fair looks urge my desire
Fain would I wed a fair young man that day and night could please me
Read, you that have some tears left yet unspent
O grief, how divers are thy shapes wherein men languish!
'Tis now dead night, and not a light on earth
Fortune and Glory may be lost and won
So parted you as if the world for ever
How like a golden dream you met and parted
When pale famine fed on thee
O poor distracted world, partly a slave
Now hath Flora robbed her bowers
Shows and nightly revels, signs of joy and peace
Triumph now with joy and mirth!
Time, that leads the fatal round

Come away; bring thy golden theft

На вічну память Котляревському (Na vichnu pamiat Kotliarevskomu)
Тече вода в синє море (Teche voda v synє more)
На що мені чорні брови (Na shcho meni chorni brovy)
Тяжко-важко в світі жити (Tiazhko-vazhko v sviti zhyty)
За думою дума роєм вилітає (Za dumoiu duma roєm vylitaє)
Минають дні, минають ночі (Mynaiut dni, mynaiut nochi)
Чого мені тяжко, чого мені нудно (Choho meni tiazhko, choho meni nudno)
Вітер в гаї нагинає лозу (Viter v hai nahynaє lozu)
Не хочу я женитися (Ne khochu ya zhenytysia)
Не женися на багатій (Ne zhenysia na bahatii)
Ой одна я одна (Oi odna ya odna)
Ой стрічечка до стрічечки (Oi strichechka do strichechky)
Не спалося, а ніч як море (Ne spalosia, a nich yak more)
Один у другого питаєм (Odyn u druhoho pytaєm)
Самому чудно, а де же дітись (Samomu chudno, a de zhe ditys)
То так і я тепер пишу (To tak i ya teper pyshu)
Чи ми ще зійдемось знову (Chy my shche ziidemos znovu)
Огні горять, музика грає (Ohni horiat, muzyka hraє)
Та не дай, Господи, нікому (Ta ne dai, Hospody, nikomu)
На батька бісового трачу (Na batka bisovoho trachu)
Ой гляну я подивлюся (Oi hlianu ya podyvliusia)
Чи то недоля та неволя (Chy to nedolia ta nevolia)
Добро, у кого є господа (Dobro, u koho є hospoda)
І золотої й дорогої (I zolotoi y dorohoi)
Ми в купочці колись росли (My v kupochtsi kolys rosly)
І станом гнучим і красою (I stanom hnuchym i krasoiu)
Ми в осені таки похожі (My v oseni taky pokhozhi)
У бога за дверьми лежала сокира (U boha za dvermy lezhala sokyra)
Не знаю, як тепер Ляхи живуть (Ne znaiu, yak teper Liakhy zhyvut)
За сонцем хмаронька пливе (Za sontsem khmaronka plyve)
Мов за подушне оступили (Mov za podushne ostupyly)
І знов мені не привезла нічого почта (I znov meni ne pryvezla nichoho pochta)
Як-би зострілися ми знову (Yak-by zostrilysia my znovu)
Як маю я журитися (Yak maiu ya zhurytysia)
Не жаль на злого (Ne zhal na zloho)
Не так тиї вороги (Ne tak tyi vorohy)
Між скалами, неначе злодій (Mizh skalamy, nenache zlodii)
Ой чого ти почорніло (Oi choho ty pochornilo)
У неділеньку у святую (U nedilenku u sviatuiu)
На велик-день на соломі (Na velyk-den na solomi)
По улиці вітер віє (Po ulytsi viter viє)
Ой умер старий батько (Oi umer staryi batko)
На улиці не весело (Na ulytsi ne veselo)
Як-би мені, мамо, намисто (Yak-by meni, mamo, namysto)
І багата я, і вродлива я (I bahata ya, i vrodlyva ya)
На городі коло броду (Na horodi kolo brodu)
Ой сяду я під хатою (Oi siadu ya pid khatoiu)
Не вернувся із походу (Ne vernuvsia iz pokhodu)
Було роблю що, чи гуляю (Bulo robliu shcho, chy huliaiu)
Ой не пьються пива-меди (Oi ne piutsia pyva-medy)
У неділеньку та ранесенько (U nedilenku ta ranesenko)
Коло гаю, в чистім полю (Kolo haiu, v chystim poliu)

Не ветер, вея с высоты… (Ne veter, veya s vysoty)
Где гнутся над омутом лозы… (Gde gnutsya nad omutom lozy)
Слеза дрожит в твоём ревнивом взоре… (Sleza drozhit v tvoyom revnivom vzore)
Пусто в покое моём. Один я сижу у камина… (Pusto v pokoe moyom. Odin ya sizhu u kamina)

He treadeth the winepress of the fierceness and wrath of Almighty God

Love loveth Thee, and wisdom loveth Thee

The Greatest of these is charity

Lord, I am feeble and of mean account
They shall be as white as snow

Grant us such grace that we may work Thy Will

Do this, and he doeth it
That no man take thy Crown

Lord, it is good for us to be here
Lord, grant us grace to rest upon Thy word
What is this above thy head
Standing afar off for the fear of her torment
O Lucifer, Son of the Morning!
As froth on the face of the deep
Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched
Toll, bell, toll. For hope is flying
Earth has clear call of daily bells
Whatsoever is right, that shall we receive
This near-at-hand land breeds pain by measure

Thou who must fall silent in a while

This banner over me was Love
Beloved, yield thy time to God, for He
The half moon shows a face of plaintive sweetness

Give thanks to-day, and let to-morrow take

Ye that fear him, both small and great
The sinner’s own fault? So it was

Laughing Life cries at the feast
Who would wish back the Saints upon our rough

I see that all things come to an end
Just thy commandment is exceeding broad
O ye, who are not dead and fit
O ye who taste that love is sweet

Now they desire a better Country
Our heaven must be within ourselves
Of all the downfalls in the world
The hills are tipped with sunshine, while I walk

That which I chose, I choose
In the day of his Espousals
She came from the uttermost part of the earth
Alleluia! or Alas! my heart is crying
The Passion Flower hath sprung up tall
The flowers appear on the Earth
One of the Soldiers with a Spear pierced his Side
Where love is, there comes sorrow

One woe is past. Come what come will
Take no thought for the morrow
Consider the Lillies of the field
Heaviness may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning
The Will of the Lord be done
Lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven
Whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth

Are ye not much better than they?

Glee! The great storm is over

Elysium is as far as to
If you were coming in the fall

There came a day at summer's full
I'm ceded, I've stopped being theirs
'T was a long parting, but the time
She rose to his requirement, dropped
New feet within my garden go
Perhaps you'd like to buy a flower

The bee is not afraid of me

A little road not made of man
A drop fell on the apple tree

This is the land the sunset washes

The mountain sat upon the plain
I'll tell you how the sun rose, --
Of all the sounds despatched abroad

She went as quiet as the dew

It was too late for man
When I was small, a woman died
The daisy follows soft the sun

I found the phrase to every thought

The thought beneath so slight a film

I should have been too glad, I see

A shady friend for torrid days

"GOING to him! Happy letter! Tell him --

Bring me the sunset in a cup

Let down the bars, O Death

I have not told my garden yet
They dropped like flakes, they dropped like stars
The only ghost I ever saw
Some, too fragile for winter winds

Triumph may be of several kinds
Pompless no life can pass away
I had no cause to be awake
On such a night, or such a night
I lived on dread; to those who know
One need not be a chamber to be haunted
She died, -- this was the way she died
Wait till the majesty of Death
Went up a year this evening
It was not death, for I stood up
I should not dare to leave my friend
Great streets of silence led away
I think just how my shape will rise
Lay this laurel on the one
'T is little I could care for pearls
Heaven is what I cannot reach
It's such a little thing to weep

We never know how high we are
While I was fearing it, it came
There is no frigate like a book

A face devoid of love or grace
From all the jails the boys and girls

Upon the gallows hung a wretch
I felt a clearing in my mind
The farthest thunder that I heard
On the bleakness of my lot
A door just opened on a street --
Fate slew him, but he did not drop
Finite to fail, but infinite to venture
I measure every grief I meet

It dropped so low in my regard

Remembrance has a rear and front, --
The brain is wider than the sky

The past is such a curious creature
You cannot put a fire out
A modest lot, a fame petite
I stepped from plank to plank
One day is there of the series
Proud of my broken heart since thou didst break it
My worthiness is all my doubt
One blessing had I, than the rest
When roses cease to bloom, dear
Summer for thee grant I may be
Split the lark and you'll find the music
To lose thee, sweeter than to gain
Father, I bring thee not myself, --
We outgrow love like other things
Not with a club the heart is broken
My friend must be a bird
He touched me, so I live to know
Let me not mar that perfect dream
I live with him, I see his face
I envy seas whereon he rides
A solemn thing it was, I said
A lady red upon the hill
We like March, his shoes are purple
Not knowing when the dawn will come
A murmur in the trees to note

To my quick ear the leaves conferred
A sepal, petal, and a thorn
High from the earth I heard a bird

Sweet is the swamp with its secrets
The moon was but a chin of gold

You've seen balloons set, haven't you
A sloop of amber slips away
How the old mountains drip with sunset
The murmuring of bees has ceased
That is solemn we have ended, --
That such have died enables us
They won't frown always, -- some sweet day
The distance that the dead have gone
'T is sunrise, little maid, hast thou
Each that we lose takes part of us
Not any higher stands the grave
As far from pity as complaint
'T is whiter than an Indian pipe
She laid her docile crescent down
Bless God, he went as soldiers
Where every bird is bold to go
The grave my little cottage is
This was in the white of the year
From us she wandered now a year
I wish I knew that woman's name
Bereaved of all, I went abroad
I felt a funeral in my brain
I meant to find her when I came
I sing to use the waiting
A sickness of this world it most occasions
So proud she was to die
Tie the strings to my life, my Lord
The dying need but little, dear, --
The soul should always stand ajar
Three weeks passed since I had seen her, --
I breathed enough to learn the trick
If tolling bell I ask the cause
If I may have it when it's dead
Before the ice is in the pools
I heard a fly buzz when I died
There's been a death in the opposite house
We never know we go, -- when we are going
We thirst at first, -- 't is Nature's act
A clock stopped -- not the mantel's
A toad can die of light
Far from love the Heavenly Father
A long, long sleep, a famous sleep
'T was just this time last year I died
A bird is of all beings
A prison gets to be a friend;
A wife at daybreak I shall be,
After great pain a formal feeling comes—
All the letters I can write
Although I put away his life,
And this of all my hopes—
As if the sea should part
By my window have I for scenery
Conscious am I in my chamber
Could I do more for thee
Don't put up my thread and needle,
Doom is the House Without the Door
Forever at his side to walk
God is a distant, stately Lover,
Heaven has different signs to me;
Heaven is so far of the mind
How many flowers fail in wood,
I've known a Heaven like a tent
I've nothing else to bring, you know,
I came to buy a smile to-day
I cannot dance upon my toes,
I cautious scanned my little life,
I fear a man of scanty speech,
I got so I could hear his name
I know lives I could miss
I make his crescent fill or lack,
I never felt at home below,
I prayed at first—a little girl—
I reckon, when I count at all,
I should not dare to be so sad
I tend my flowers for thee,
I tie my hat, I crease my shawl,
I took one draught of life,
